papers.summary: Given a positive, non-increasing sequence $a$ with sum $1$, we consider the family $\mathcal{C}_a$ of closed subsets of $[0,1]$ whose complementary open intervals have lengths given by the terms of $a$. We study which functions $θ\mapsto\overline{\dim}_{\,θ}E$ arise as the upper intermediate dimensions of sets $E\in\mathcal{C}_a$. Under a natural condition on the decay of $a$, we show that these are exactly the functions in the class introduced by Banaji and Rutar that take the value $\overline{\dim}_{\rm B}C_a$ at $θ=1$ and are bounded above by the upper intermediate dimensions of the decreasing Cantor set $C_a$. We also show that the lower bound given by the countable set $D_a$ is rigid: if it is attained at one value of $θ$, then it is attained at all larger values.
papers.title: Attainable forms of intermediate dimensions of complementary sets

papers.summary: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.
papers.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures

papers.summary: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.
papers.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations

papers.summary: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials. The proof uses polynomial transformations that preserve zeros in a real interval and in the unit disk. As an application, we prove that the extended Turán expressions for the Bell polynomials are weakly Hurwitz stable. We also prove the corresponding result for the reflected Laguerre polynomials using polynomial approximations. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai.
papers.title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials

papers.summary: We prove accelerated mixing for a Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin sampler: the OBABO splitting with friction $2\sqrt m$, adjusted with Neal's non-reversibly updated uniform, which is redrawn after every epoch of $E$ steps. For targets $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $mI\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq LI$ and an $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian, started from a Gaussian at an approximate minimizer, the chain reaches total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ after $\tilde O\big(\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}(d/m)^{3/4}\big)$ gradient evaluations, where $κ=L/m$ and $\tilde O$ hides logarithmic factors. The $\sqrtκ$ term is necessary, already on Gaussian targets. The proof discretizes Lu's entropic hypocoercivity by means of an entropy inequality for free transport, so that the relative entropy of the unadjusted chain decays at a rate of order $\sqrt m$ up to a discretization bias. With the non-reversibly updated uniform, the leading energy errors of velocity Verlet telescope along a path. A coupling argument combines the two. On Bayesian logistic regression posteriors for two standard data sets, which satisfy these assumptions, the gradient cost of the chain with the non-reversibly updated uniform grows roughly like the square root of the condition number at the posterior mode, and that of standard adjusted OBABO roughly like its $3/4$ power.
papers.title: Persistence Pays: Square-root condition-number dependence for Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin Monte Carlo with a non-reversibly updated accept/reject uniform

papers.summary: A permutation $σ\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $σ(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k σ(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $Φ_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $Φ_p = Φ_p^{+} \sqcup Φ_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| Φ_p^{+} | - | Φ_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $σ\inΦ_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $Φ_p^{+}$ versus $Φ_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $σ^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.
papers.title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$

papers.summary: The validity problem for first-order logic is a well-known undecidable problem. The undecidability also holds even for $\mathsf{FO}3$ and (equational formulas of) the calculus of relations. In this paper we tighten these undecidability results to the following: (1) $\mathsf{FO}3$ with just one binary relation is undecidable even without equality; and (2) the calculus of relations with just one character and with only composition, union, and complement is undecidable. Additionally we prove that the finite validity problem is also undecidable for the above two classes.
papers.title: The Undecidability of FO3 and the Calculus of Relations with Just One Binary Relation

papers.summary: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,θ}$ boundary, $0<θ\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.
papers.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels

papers.summary: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. This work constructs multi-fidelity particle flow filters by augmenting a small number of expensive high-fidelity particles (full-order model runs) with a large number of inexpensive low-resolution particles (reduced-order surrogates constructed via intrusive Galerkin projection). These surrogates act as control variates to enhance the statistical estimate of the full-order posterior, yielding enhanced analysis accuracy at comparable computational cost. The work focuses on two particle flows based on log homotopy, the stochastic Gromov flow and deterministic Exact flow. Numerical experiments with the Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) and Quasi-Geostrophic (QG) test problems demonstrate that the proposed MFPFF achieves accuracy comparable to high-fidelity simulations while significantly reducing computational expense.
papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy

papers.summary: We present a method for computing a specific type of matrix decomposition that combines a structured framework with data-driven adaptation. This framework allows for an efficient and stable representation of signals or images using frames by identifying sets of vectors that naturally capture the essential features of the given data. The resulting decomposition enables the development of regularization techniques that enhance the quality of reconstruction by preserving important signal characteristics while suppressing noise. We develop an optimization-based algorithm to compute the decomposition and establish convergence properties of the resulting iterates. Numerical experiments on synthetic data and tomographic image reconstruction illustrate the behavior of the proposed method and its performance compared to conventional spectral regularization methods.
papers.title: Computing Data-Aware Diagonal Frame Decompositions

papers.summary: Solutions to elliptic boundary value problems on three-dimensional nonsmooth domains exhibit singular behavior near edges and vertices. Using layer potential theory, we investigate boundary integral equations for the Laplace equation and characterize the leading singular exponents of the surface density on conical domains. For two canonical geometries, we derive explicit formulas for the two families of edge singular exponents on a dihedral wedge, and characterize the modewise vertex singular exponents on an axisymmetric circular cone through the zeros of associated Legendre functions and their derivatives. Building on these two prototypes and the dilation-invariance property, we formulate the associated operator pencil for general conical domains and develop a nonlinear eigenvalue solver. This solver employs the Nyström method with graded meshes, logarithmically corrected trapezoidal rules, and Brent's method to compute these singular exponents accurately and efficiently. Numerical examples for trihedral cones, regular m-hedral cones, and droplet-type cones verify the effectiveness of our approach and illustrate the interactions between edge and vertex singularities.
papers.title: Singularity Analysis of Laplace Boundary Integral Equations on Three-Dimensional Domains with Corners

papers.summary: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg's universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.
papers.title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue

papers.summary: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_θ$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_θ$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.
papers.title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits

papers.summary: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.
papers.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields

papers.summary: We overview recent results quantifying the Besicovitch projection theorem, focusing on the theory of quantitative rectifiability and connection to Vitushkin's conjecture.
papers.title: Survey on Favard length and rectifiability

papers.summary: We prove that a quiver potential over a field of characteristic zero is finitely determined if and only if the trace space of its Jacobian algebra is finite dimensional. In particular, Jacobi-finite potentials are finitely determined. We further prove that rigid potentials are finitely determined and, over an algebraically closed field, unique up to right equivalence on a fixed quiver. For finitely determined weighted-homogeneous potentials, we give an explicit bound on the jet order sufficient for finite determinacy in terms of the arrow weights, the weight of the potential, and the highest nonzero weight of the trace space of its Jacobian algebra. We also establish new invariance results for weighted-homogeneous potentials under right equivalence.
papers.title: Finite determinacy and rigidity of quiver potentials

papers.summary: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(τ_1, \ldots, τ_n, j(τ_1), \ldots, j(τ_n)) \in V$ with $τ_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouché's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
papers.title: Modular Existential Closedness

papers.summary:
We determine the Borel-reducibility comparison of each pair of $\mathbfΠ^0_3$ benchmark equivalence relations in Gao's monograph. The additional comparisons we prove are $E_\infty\leq_B c_0$, $E_\infty
leq_B\ell_p$ for $2<p<\infty$, $\ell_p
leq_B{\equiv_m}$ for $2<p<\infty$, $c_0
leq_B{\equiv_m}$, $c_0
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$ and $\equiv_m
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$. Together with the previous positive direction, these give $\ell_p\leq_B{\equiv_m}$ if and only if $p\leq2$. These answer several questions in Gao's monograph and Kanovei' monograph. We also prove that unitary equivalence of all bounded linear operators is not Borel reducible to $\equiv_m$. This answers a question of Ding and Gao. Equivalently, unitary equivalence of arbitrary representations of $F_\infty$ is strictly more complicated than that of arbitrary representations of $\mathbb Z$. This answers a question of Thomas.
papers.title: Comparisons of benchmark equivalence relations

papers.summary: We show that if $κ^{<κ} = κ$, then there is a $κ$-strategically closed, $κ^+$-c.c.\ partial order that forces $\square_κ$. We discuss consequences for generic large cardinals.
papers.title: Forcing square with small conditions

papers.summary: What does a recursive definition mean when the logic is grounded, so a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? Kripke's answer for the special case of truth was the least fixed point. This paper takes that answer as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) already writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term, paradoxes included. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, so that accessibility, the winning positions of a game, and grounded truth itself each come with their own induction principle. The rule is sound for the omega model and the system is consistent, both machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL. With the rule, IGA proves Goodstein's theorem outright, in a logic without implication at an undecided hypothesis, and the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, both with every step of the arithmetic a grounded derivation. It proves the Cantor normal forms well-founded, from which the well-foundedness of the standard $\varepsilon_0$ notation system in HOL follows, and it certifies the Veblen notation as an ordinal below every $\varphi(n,0)$. It defines Kripke truth for RGA's own language as one fixed point that agrees with the omega model exactly. Two equivalences locate what the classical world has and the grounded one does not. IGA proves the whole Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for that order, and bivalence of accessibility for an order is sound exactly when the order is well-founded; so $Γ_0$ lies at most one instance of excluded middle away, at the accessibility predicate of the notation, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in a primitive-recursive form of Kleene's $\mathcal O$ are interderivable over IGA.
papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $Γ_0$
